issue.title: v1-to-v2 adoption leaves orphaned imported v1 chat files on disk
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-w2.4 (epic sase-w2, v2-adoption) as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #1; corroborated by sase-w2.land on 2026-09-04 while landing the epic.

When v1-to-v2 adoption refreshes a matched v1 artifact in place and the adopted run has its own v2 chat, the old v1 chat copy (~/chats/<shard>/imported-<name>-<ts>.md) stays on disk with no remaining referrer — its only referrer was the v1 agent_meta.json that adoption rewrote. 338 such files were observed on the wedged machine (kellys_mbp) that motivated the epic.

Remediation: a sweep (likely as part of adoption or a maintenance pass) that reclaims chat files whose only referrer was a v1 agent_meta.json rewritten by adoption. Deletion must be evidence-gated the same way adoption is: only reclaim when the rewritten meta provably pointed at the file and the adopted run's v2 chat is present.

task_type_fields.impact: Unbounded stale chat files accumulate after adoption; duplicate copies of the same run's chat confuse chat browsing and waste disk
task_type_fields.repro: Run sase agent sync on a machine with v1-imported agents whose adopted runs carry their own v2 chat; the old imported-*.md chat copies remain on disk unreferenced (338 observed on kellys_mbp)
